blocks.raw: > Akamai's Application Security API allows you to access and modify your Security Configurations for Kona Site Defender, Web Application Protector, App & API Protector, Advanced Security Module, and Client Reputation. You can create, update, activate, and export versions of a security configuration. You can get selectable hostnames and add them to the selected list to protect your website or API content. You also can add, modify, or delete custom rules and assign policy actions.
blocks.text: Akamai's Application Security API allows you to access and modify your Security Configurations for Kona Site Defender, Web Application Protector, App & API Protector, Advanced Security Module, and Client Reputation. You can create, update, activate, and export versions of a security configuration. You can get selectable hostnames and add them to the selected list to protect your website or API content. You also can add, modify, or delete custom rules and assign policy actions.

blocks.raw:
- [Clone or create a security policy](https://techdocs.akamai.com/application-security/reference/post-policy.md): __Kona Site Defender__, __App & API Protector with the Advanced Security module__ Creates a new copy of an existing security policy or creates a new security policy from scratch when you don't specify a policy to clone in the request. To create a new security policy, leave `createFromSecurityPolicy` empty in your request.
- [List security policies](https://techdocs.akamai.com/application-security/reference/get-policies.md): __All products__ Returns a list of security policies available for the specified security configuration.
- [Get a security policy](https://techdocs.akamai.com/application-security/reference/get-policy.md): __All products__ Returns the specified security policy.
- [Modify a security policy](https://techdocs.akamai.com/application-security/reference/put-policy.md): __All products__ Update the name of a specific security policy. Currently, you can only edit a security policy's name with this operation, although other editable fields will be available in the future. For any changes to settings within a security policy, run the modify operation for that specific setting. For example, to update your IP/Geo settings, run [Update IP/Geo Firewall settings](ref:put-policy-ip-geo-firewall).
- [Remove a security policy](https://techdocs.akamai.com/application-security/reference/delete-policy.md): __Kona Site Defender__, __App & API Protector with the Advanced Security module__ Delete the specified security policy. You can't delete a security policy that is actively in use. Before you run this operation, create a new version of your security configuration and omit the policy you want to delete. Once you have activated your new configuration version, you can delete the security policy you omitted from the new version. One way to create a new configuration quickly is to run [Clone a configuration version](ref:post-config-versions), remove the policy you want to delete, then PUT the edited object back to [Modify a security policy](ref:put-policy).
- [List rate policy actions](https://techdocs.akamai.com/application-security/reference/get-rate-policies-actions.md): __All products__ Returns a list of all rate policies currently in use with the actions each policy takes when conditions are met.
- [Modify a rate policy action](https://techdocs.akamai.com/application-security/reference/put-rate-policy-action.md): __All products__ Updates the actions in a rate policy.
- [Get IP/Geo Firewall settings](https://techdocs.akamai.com/application-security/reference/get-policy-ip-geo-firewall.md): __All products__ Lists which network lists are used in the IP/Geo Firewall settings. In Control Center this method is called `mode`. In this API the method is called `blocked`. The response shows blocked and allowed IPs depending on which network lists you include and which version of the mode you choose. If you want to add or remove IP addresses from the network lists, use the [Network Lists API](https://techdocs.akamai.com/network-lists/reference/api). Note that subnet controls are a legacy item in Control Center and are not available through this API.
- [Modify IP/Geo Firewall settings](https://techdocs.akamai.com/application-security/reference/put-policy-ip-geo-firewall.md): __All products__ Update the method and which network lists to use for IP/Geo firewall blocking. In Control Center this method is called `mode`. In this API the method is called `blocked`. Use `blockSpecificIPGeo` to block any IPs, geographies, or network lists you choose with this setting. Use `blockAllTrafficExceptAllowedIPs` to allow specific IPs or geographies that you choose to let through while the rest remain blocked. IPs you want to allow are contained in the `allowedIPNetworkLists`. It's important to verify the IPs you block are the ones you intend to block as it's easy to block wanted traffic by accident. Note that subnet controls are a legacy item in Control Center and are not available through this API.
- [Get attack payload logging settings for a policy](https://techdocs.akamai.com/application-security/reference/get-policies-attack-payload-logging.md): __All products__ List a security policy's settings for attack payload logging. Attack payload logging is on by default, and in most cases you should leave it enabled. When set to `NONE`, the request body and response body appear as `redacted` in the log. For example, `JSON_PAIRS:redacted`. This operation applies at the security policy level, and overrides the attack payload logging settings at the configuration level on a per-policy basis.
- [Modify attack payload logging settings for a policy](https://techdocs.akamai.com/application-security/reference/put-policies-attack-payload-logging.md): __All products__ Update attack payload logging settings for a specific policy. This operation applies at the security policy level, and overrides the attack payload logging settings at the configuration level on a per-policy basis. When set to `NONE`, the request body and response body appear as `redacted` in the log. For example, `JSON_PAIRS:redacted`.
- [Get HTTP header log settings](https://techdocs.akamai.com/application-security/reference/get-policies-logging.md): __All products__ List a security policy's settings for HTTP header logging. HTTP header logging is on by default, and in most cases you should leave it enabled. You can filter requests by header type, including or excluding requests with a specific header, or by cookie. This operation applies at the security policy level, and overrides the HTTP header log settings at the configuration level on a per-policy basis.
- [Modify HTTP header log settings](https://techdocs.akamai.com/application-security/reference/put-policies-logging.md): __All products__ Enable, disable, or update HTTP header logging settings for a specific policy. This operation applies at the security policy level, and overrides the HTTP header log settings at the configuration level on a per-policy basis.
- [List reputation profile actions](https://techdocs.akamai.com/application-security/reference/get-reputation-profiles-actions.md): __Kona Site Defender__, __App & API Protector with the Advanced Security module__ Return a list of reputation profiles with their associated actions.
- [Get the action for a reputation profile](https://techdocs.akamai.com/application-security/reference/get-reputation-profile-action.md): __Kona Site Defender__, __App & API Protector with the Advanced Security module__ Return the action a reputation profile takes when triggered.
- [Modify the action for a reputation profile](https://techdocs.akamai.com/application-security/reference/put-reputation-profile-action.md): __Kona Site Defender__, __App & API Protector with the Advanced Security module__ Update what action to take when reputation profile's rule triggers. Use `alert` to record the trigger of the event, `deny` to block the request, or `none` to take no action. Currently the only field in the reputation profile object is `action`.
- [List custom rule actions](https://techdocs.akamai.com/application-security/reference/get-custom-rules.md): __All products__ Returns a list of all configured custom rules for the specified configuration. It includes information for rules that are associated with this policy, as well as the latest versions of the rules in the configuration that aren't associated with the current policy. Unassociated rules have an action of `none`.
- [Modify a custom rule action](https://techdocs.akamai.com/application-security/reference/put-custom-rule.md): __All products__ Updates the action of a custom rule.
- [Get reputation analysis settings](https://techdocs.akamai.com/application-security/reference/get-reputation-analysis.md): __Kona Site Defender__ Return the current reputation analysis settings.
- [Modify reputation analysis settings](https://techdocs.akamai.com/application-security/reference/put-reputation-analysis.md): __Kona Site Defender__ Toggle the `forwardToHTTPHeader` and `forwardSharedIPToHTTPHeaderAndSIEM` options. The `forwardToHTTPHeader` option adds client reputation details to requests forwarded to origin in an HTTP header. The `forwardSharedIPToHTTPHeaderAndSIEM` option adds a value indicating that shared IPs are included in HTTP header and SIEM integration when used.
- [List URL protection policy actions](https://techdocs.akamai.com/application-security/reference/get-url-protection-policies-actions.md): __All products__ Returns a list of all URL protection policies currently in use, along with the actions each policy takes when conditions are met.
- [Modify a URL protection policy action](https://techdocs.akamai.com/application-security/reference/put-url-protection-policy-action.md): __All products__ Updates the actions in a URL protection policy.
- [Get Pragma settings for a security policy](https://techdocs.akamai.com/application-security/reference/get-policies-pragma-header.md): __All products__ Return the `Pragma` header's excluded conditions. By default, the `Pragma` header debugging information is stripped from an operation's response except in cases where you set `excludeCondition`. This operation applies at the security policy level. To modify `Pragma` header settings at the security configuration level, run [List Pragma header settings for a configuration](ref:get-advanced-settings-pragma-header).
- [Modify Pragma settings for a security policy](https://techdocs.akamai.com/application-security/reference/put-policies-pragma-header.md): __All products__ Update the pragma header excluded conditions. By default, the `Pragma` header debugging information is stripped from an operation's response except in cases where you set `excludeCondition`. To remove existing settings, submit your request with an empty payload `{}` at the top-level of an object. For example, submit `"type": "{}"` in the request body to remove the `requestHeaderValueMatch` from the excluded conditions. If you submit an empty payload for each field, you'll clear all of your condition settings. To modify `Pragma` header settings at the security configuration level, run [Modify Pragma header settings for a configuration](ref:put-advanced-settings-pragma-header) .
- [List API request constraints and actions](https://techdocs.akamai.com/application-security/reference/get-api-request-constraints.md): __Kona Site Defender__, __App & API Protector with the Advanced Security module__ Return a list of APIs with their constraints and associated actions.
- [Modify the request constraint action for all APIs](https://techdocs.akamai.com/application-security/reference/put-api-request-constraints.md): __Kona Site Defender__, __App & API Protector with the Advanced Security module__ Update what action to take when any API request constraint triggers. Use `alert` to record the trigger of the event, `deny` to block the request, or `customDenyId` to apply a custom deny response.
- [Modify an API request constraint's action](https://techdocs.akamai.com/application-security/reference/put-api-request-constraints-api.md): __Kona Site Defender__, __App & API Protector with the Advanced Security module__ Update what action to take when the API request constraint triggers. This operation modifies an individual API constraint action. To use this operation, run [List all API request constraints and actions](ref:get-api-request-constraints) and pick an API from the response list. Use `alert` to record the trigger of the event, `deny` to block the request, or `none` to take no action. Currently the only field in the API Request Constraints object is `action`.
- [Get evasive path match settings](https://techdocs.akamai.com/application-security/reference/get-evasive-path-match.md): __Web Application Protector__, __Kona Site Defender__ Lists the evasive path match setting for a security policy. Evasive path match is off by default. This setting applies at the security policy level and overrides the setting at the configuration level on a per-policy basis.
- [Modify evasive path match settings](https://techdocs.akamai.com/application-security/reference/put-evasive-path-match.md): __Web Application Protector__, __Kona Site Defender__ Enable, disable, or update evasive path match setting for a security policy. This operation applies at the security policy level and overrides the setting at the configuration level on a per-policy basis.
- [List malware policy actions](https://techdocs.akamai.com/application-security/reference/get-malware-policies-actions.md): __All products__ Return a list of all malware policies currently in use with the actions each policy takes when conditions are met.
- [Modify a malware policy action](https://techdocs.akamai.com/application-security/reference/put-malware-policy-action.md): __All products__ Update the actions in a malware policy.
- [Get request body inspection limit settings for a security policy](https://techdocs.akamai.com/application-security/reference/get-policies-request-body.md): __All products__ Return request body inspection limit settings for a security policy. Contact your account team if you'd like to run this operation.
- [Modify request body size settings for a security policy](https://techdocs.akamai.com/application-security/reference/put-policies-request-body.md): __All products__ Update inspection settings for a security policy. Inspect request bodies up to a certain size. In exceptional cases, you can change the default value to a set limit: `8`, `16`, or `32` KB. Contact your account team if you'd like to run this operation.
- [List API endpoints](https://techdocs.akamai.com/application-security/reference/get-api-endpoints.md): __Kona Site Defender__, __App & API Protector with the Advanced Security module__ List the API endpoints associated with a security policy. This operation only lists the endpoints. To manage them, use [Register an endpoint](https://techdocs.akamai.com/api-gateway/reference/post-endpoints) from the API Endpoint Definition API.
- [Get slow POST protection settings](https://techdocs.akamai.com/application-security/reference/get-policy-slow-post.md): __All products__ Get slow POST protection settings for a specific policy.
- [Modify slow POST protection settings](https://techdocs.akamai.com/application-security/reference/put-policy-slow-post.md): __All products__ Update slow POST protection settings for a specific policy.
- [List rules](https://techdocs.akamai.com/application-security/reference/get-policy-rules.md): __Kona Site Defender__, __App & API Protector with the Advanced Security module__ Returns the action taken for each rule in a policy. The action occurs when the rules are triggered by a request. These are not the same rules as Custom Rules that you configure yourself. These rules are maintained by Akamai.
- [Upgrade KRS ruleset](https://techdocs.akamai.com/application-security/reference/put-policy-rules.md): __Kona Site Defender__, __App & API Protector with the Advanced Security module__, __Adaptive Security Engine__ Upgrade to the most recent version of the KRS rule set. Akamai periodically updates these rules to keep protections current. However, the rules you use in your security policies do not automatically upgrade to the latest version when setting `mode` to `KRS`. These rules do update automatically when you have `mode` set to `AAG`. Before you upgrade, run [Get upgrade details](ref:get-rules-upgrade-details) to see which rules have changed. If you want to test how these rules would operate with live traffic before committing to the upgrade, run them in evaluation mode. This applies to KRS rules only and does not allow you to make any changes to the rules themselves. The response is the same as the `mode` response. If you're already using or want to switch from KRS to Adaptive Security Engine (ASE), pass `"upgrade": true,` and `"mode": "ASE_AUTO"` or `ASE_MANUAL` in your request. If you're using Kona Rule Sets, continue to pass only the upgrade value. Note that this operation does not grant access to Adaptive Security Engine. It updates the ASE protections if you already have ASE on your contract. Once you switch to ASE protections, you can't go back to KRS rules. Contact your account team if you want to add ASE to your contract.
- [Get upgrade details](https://techdocs.akamai.com/application-security/reference/get-rules-upgrade-details.md): __Kona Site Defender__, __App & API Protector with the Advanced Security module__ Only applies to Kona rule sets. The KRS rule sets are maintained by Akamai's security research team. Run this operation before you upgrade to verify changes in the rule sets. If you want to test how the updates affect your site, you can run the updated rules in evaluation mode.
- [Get the action for a rule](https://techdocs.akamai.com/application-security/reference/get-rule.md): __Kona Site Defender__, __App & API Protector with the Advanced Security module__ Return the action a rule takes when triggered. This applies to both ASE auto and ASE manual upgrade modes. Rule actions for `ASE_AUTO` are currently in beta. Contact your account team to access this option.
- [Modify the action for a rule](https://techdocs.akamai.com/application-security/reference/put-rule.md): __Kona Site Defender__, __App & API Protector with the Advanced Security module__ Update what action a rule takes when it's triggered. This applies to both ASE auto and ASE manual upgrade modes. Rule actions for `ASE_AUTO` are currently in beta. Contact your account team to access this option. Use `alert` to record the trigger of the event, `deny` to block the request, or `none` to take no action.
- [Get the conditions and exceptions of a rule](https://techdocs.akamai.com/application-security/reference/get-rule-condition-exception.md): __Kona Site Defender__, __App & API Protector with the Advanced Security module__ List a KRS rule's conditions and exceptions.
- [Modify the conditions and exceptions of a rule](https://techdocs.akamai.com/application-security/reference/put-rule-condition-exception.md): __Kona Site Defender__, __App & API Protector with the Advanced Security module__ Update a rule's conditions and exceptions. When the conditions are met, the rule's actions are ignored and _not_ applied to that specific traffic.
- [Get adaptive intelligence settings](https://techdocs.akamai.com/application-security/reference/get-rules-threat-intel.md): __All products__ Returns whether adaptive intelligence is enabled. Adaptive intelligence allows our network to better tune rules for better accuracy. Contact your account team if you'd like to run this operation.
- [Modify adaptive intelligence settings](https://techdocs.akamai.com/application-security/reference/put-rules-threat-intel.md): __All products__ Only applies to Adaptive Security Engine (ASE) manual rule sets. Enable or disable adaptive intelligence. Contact your account team if you'd like to run this operation.
- [Get a security policy's rule set](https://techdocs.akamai.com/application-security/reference/get-waf-policy-ruleset-composite.md): __All products__ Returns the security policy rule set, which includes the version, threat intelligence settings, rules, and attack group details.
- [Modify a security policy's rule set](https://techdocs.akamai.com/application-security/reference/patch-waf-policy-ruleset-composite.md): __All products__ Modify the security policy's rule set including its rule and attack group details.
- [Get protections](https://techdocs.akamai.com/application-security/reference/get-policy-protections.md): __All products__ Get the protections and whether they are enabled or disabled in a security policy.
- [Modify protections](https://techdocs.akamai.com/application-security/reference/put-policy-protections.md): __All products__ Update the security policy protections. This applies a set of protections that you can enable individually.
- [Get the penalty box](https://techdocs.akamai.com/application-security/reference/get-policy-penalty-box.md): __All products__ Returns the penalty box settings for the security policy you specify.
- [Modify the penalty box](https://techdocs.akamai.com/application-security/reference/put-policy-penalty-box.md): __All products__ Modifies the penalty box settings for a security policy. When the penalty box is enabled for a policy, clients that trigger a WAF Deny action are placed in the _penalty box_. There, the action you select for penalty box (either `Alert` or `Deny`) continues to apply to any requests from that client for the next 10 minutes.
- [Get penalty box condition](https://techdocs.akamai.com/application-security/reference/get-policy-penalty-box-conditions.md): __All products__ Returns the penalty box condition settings for a security policy.
- [Modify the penalty box conditions](https://techdocs.akamai.com/application-security/reference/put-policy-penalty-box-conditions.md): __All products__ Modifies the penalty box conditions settings for a security policy.
- [Respond to exception recommendations](https://techdocs.akamai.com/application-security/reference/post-recommendations.md): __Adaptive Security Engine__ Accept, decline, or reset the recommended exception. Accepting a tuning recommendation creates or updates the exception for the attack group. Use `reset` to restore a declined recommendation to a neutral state so you can accept it or decline it again later.
- [Get tuning recommendations for a policy](https://techdocs.akamai.com/application-security/reference/get-recommendations.md): __Adaptive Security Engine__ Lists available tuning recommendations for a policy. Our system can identify patterns of false positives, and suggests exceptions for you to include in your policy.
- [List tuning recommendations for an attack group](https://techdocs.akamai.com/application-security/reference/get-attack-group.md): __Adaptive Security Engine__ Returns available tuning recommendations for an attack group. Our system can identify patterns of false positives, and suggests exceptions for you to include in your attack group.
- [List tuning recommendations for a rule](https://techdocs.akamai.com/application-security/reference/get-recommendations-rule.md): __Adaptive Security Engine__ Returns available tuning recommendations for a rule. Our system can identify patterns of false positives, and suggests exceptions for you to include in your rule. In cases where your rules are already optimum, the response payload returns empty.
- [List attack groups for a policy](https://techdocs.akamai.com/application-security/reference/get-policy-attack-groups.md): __All products__ Return a list of attack groups with their associated actions.
- [Get the action for an attack group](https://techdocs.akamai.com/application-security/reference/get-policy-attack-group.md): __All products__ Currently the only field in the response object is `action`, which displays the action for the attack group.
- [Modify the action for an attack group](https://techdocs.akamai.com/application-security/reference/put-attack-group.md): __All products__ Update what action to take when an attack group's rule triggers. Use `alert` to record the trigger of the event, `deny` to block the request, or `none` to take no action. Currently the only field in the attack group object is `action`.
- [Get the exceptions of an attack group](https://techdocs.akamai.com/application-security/reference/get-attack-group-condition-exception.md): __All products__ List an attack group's exceptions.
- [Modify the exceptions of an attack group](https://techdocs.akamai.com/application-security/reference/put-attack-group-condition-exception.md): __All products__ Update an attack group exceptions.
- [Get the current mode](https://techdocs.akamai.com/application-security/reference/get-policy-mode.md): __All products__ When using Web Application Firewall in your security policy, this mode conveys how you're planning to keep the rules up to date, either `KRS` for manual updates or `AAG` for automatic updates. This operation returns which mode your rules are currently set to.
- [Modify the mode](https://techdocs.akamai.com/application-security/reference/put-policy-mode.md): __Kona Site Defender__, __App & API Protector with the Advanced Security module__, __Adaptive Security Engine__ The mode you set determines how your rule sets are updated. Use `KRS` mode to update the rule sets manually, or `AAG` to have them update automatically. If you're using Adaptive Security Engine, use `ASE_AUTO` to update the rules automatically, or `ASE_MANUAL` to update them yourself.
- [List rapid rules](https://techdocs.akamai.com/application-security/reference/get-policy-rapid-rules.md): __All products__ Returns rapid rules. [Rapid rules](https://techdocs.akamai.com/app-api-protector/docs/rapid-rules) are WAF rules we are actively testing and refining. You can start using them while we revise them. Once we complete fine-tuning a rule, it becomes a WAF rule you can access through [List rules](doc:get-policy-rules).
- [Get rapid rules' default action](https://techdocs.akamai.com/application-security/reference/get-policy-rapid-rules-action.md): __All products__ Returns the default action set for all rapid rules. To override this setting for an individual rule, run [Update a rapid rule's action](doc:put-policy-rapid-rule-action).
- [Update rapid rules' default action](https://techdocs.akamai.com/application-security/reference/put-policy-rapid-rules-action.md): __All products__ Set rapid rules default action. This applies to _all_ rapid rules by default unless you specifically override this setting for an individual rule with [Update a rapid rule's action](doc:put-policy-rapid-rule-action).
- [Get rapid rules' status](https://techdocs.akamai.com/application-security/reference/get-policy-rapid-rules-status.md): __All products__ Returns whether rapid rules are enabled or disabled.
- [Update rapid rules' status](https://techdocs.akamai.com/application-security/reference/put-policy-rapid-rules-status.md): __All products__ Enable or disable all rapid rules.
- [List a rapid rule's conditions and exceptions](https://techdocs.akamai.com/application-security/reference/get-policy-rapid-rule-condition-exception.md): __All products__ Returns the conditions and exceptions set for the rapid rule.
- [Update a rapid rule's conditions and exceptions](https://techdocs.akamai.com/application-security/reference/put-policy-rapid-rule-condition-exception.md): __All products__ Set the rapid rule's conditions and exceptions.
- [Get a rapid rule's lock status](https://techdocs.akamai.com/application-security/reference/get-policy-rapid-rule-lock.md): __All products__ Returns the rapid rule lock status. When locked, the action set for the rapid rule applies to all new versions of that rule.
- [Update a rapid rule's lock status](https://techdocs.akamai.com/application-security/reference/put-policy-rapid-rule-lock.md): __All products__ Set the rapid rule lock status. When enabled, the action set for the rapid rule applies to all new versions of that rule.
- [Get a rapid rule's action](https://techdocs.akamai.com/application-security/reference/get-policy-rapid-rule-action.md): __All products__ Returns the action for a single rapid rule. Run [Update a rapid rule's action](doc:put-policy-rapid-rule-action) if you want to set different actions for each rule, or override the default action for a single rule.
- [Update a rapid rule's action](https://techdocs.akamai.com/application-security/reference/put-policy-rapid-rule-action.md): __All products__ Set the rapid rule's action. Run this operation if you want to set different actions for each rule, or override the default action for a single rule.
- [List AI rules](https://techdocs.akamai.com/application-security/reference/get-policy-ai-rules.md): __All products__ Returns all AI rules for the security policy. AI rules are WAF rules generated and refined using machine learning.
- [Get AI rules status](https://techdocs.akamai.com/application-security/reference/get-policy-ai-rules-status.md): __All products__ Returns whether AI rules are enabled for the security policy.
- [Update AI rules status](https://techdocs.akamai.com/application-security/reference/put-policy-ai-rules-status.md): __All products__ Enable or disable all AI rules for the security policy.
- [Get an AI rule's action](https://techdocs.akamai.com/application-security/reference/get-policy-ai-rule-action.md): __All products__ Returns the action for the specified AI rule.
- [Update an AI rule's action](https://techdocs.akamai.com/application-security/reference/put-policy-ai-rule-action.md): __All products__ Update the action for an AI rule.
- [Create a challenge action](https://techdocs.akamai.com/application-security/reference/post-challenge-action.md): Create a new challenge action. Use this action type to insert a challenge, like a CAPTCHA, into the user workflow. You can also apply your own branding to the action to match your website. See [Challenge actions](https://techdocs.akamai.com/app-api-protector/docs/challenge-actions) for more details.
- [List challenge actions](https://techdocs.akamai.com/application-security/reference/get-challenge-actions.md): List all of your challenge actions along with their names, challenge types, and other summary information.
- [Get a challenge action](https://techdocs.akamai.com/application-security/reference/get-challenge-action.md): View details about the specified challenge action.
- [Update a challenge action](https://techdocs.akamai.com/application-security/reference/put-challenge-action.md): Edit the specified challenge action, such as the name, type of challenge, or branding.
- [Delete a challenge action](https://techdocs.akamai.com/application-security/reference/delete-challenge-action.md): Remove the specified challenge action.
- [Update Google reCAPTCHA secret key](https://techdocs.akamai.com/application-security/reference/put-google-recaptcha-secret-key.md): Specify a different Google reCAPTCHA secret key for a challenge action. The secret key authorizes communication between your site and the reCAPTCHA server.
- [List Behavioral DDoS profile actions](https://techdocs.akamai.com/application-security/reference/get-behavioral-ddos-actions.md): Returns a list of all Behavioral DDoS profiles currently in use, along with the actions each profile takes when conditions are met. _Products:_ All.
- [Modify a Behavioral DDoS profile action](https://techdocs.akamai.com/application-security/reference/put-behavioral-ddos-profile-action.md): Updates the actions in a Behavioral DDoS profile. _Products:_ All.
- [Get the bypass network lists settings for a security policy](https://techdocs.akamai.com/application-security/reference/get-bypass-network-lists-per-policy.md): __Web Application Protector__, __App & API Protector__ Lists which network lists are used in the bypass network lists settings. - [Modify the bypass network lists settings for a security policy](https://techdocs.akamai.com/application-security/reference/put-bypass-network-lists-per-policy.md): __Web Application Protector__, __App & API Protector__ Update which network lists to use in the bypass network lists settings. If you want to add or remove IP addresses from the network lists, use the [Network Lists API](https://techdocs.akamai.com/network-lists/reference/api).
- [Get Client-Side Protection & Compliance settings](https://techdocs.akamai.com/application-security/reference/get-policy-cpc.md): __All products__ Get Client-Side Protection & Compliance settings for a specific policy. - [Modify Client-Side Protections & Compliance settings](https://techdocs.akamai.com/application-security/reference/put-policy-cpc.md): __All products__ Update Client-Side Protection & Compliance settings for a specific policy.

- [Modify selected hostnames for a security policy](https://techdocs.akamai.com/application-security/reference/put-selected-hostnames-per-config.md): __Web Application Protector__, __App & API Protector__ Update the list of selected hostnames for a configuration. You can add an individual hostname to your selected hostnames list without passing the entire list plus the new hostname in this PUT object. blocks.text: Clone or create a security policy: Kona Site Defender, App & API Protector with the Advanced Security module Creates a new copy of an existing security policy or creates a new security policy from scratch when you don't specify a policy to clone in the request. To create a new security policy, leave createFromSecurityPolicy empty in your request.List security policies: All products Returns a list of security policies available for the specified security configuration.Get a security policy: All products Returns the specified security policy.Modify a security policy: All products Update the name of a specific security policy. Currently, you can only edit a security policy's name with this operation, although other editable fields will be available in the future. For any changes to settings within a security policy, run the modify operation for that specific setting. For example, to update your IP/Geo settings, run Update IP/Geo Firewall settings.Remove a security policy: Kona Site Defender, App & API Protector with the Advanced Security module Delete the specified security policy. You can't delete a security policy that is actively in use. Before you run this operation, create a new version of your security configuration and omit the policy you want to delete. Once you have activated your new configuration version, you can delete the security policy you omitted from the new version. One way to create a new configuration quickly is to run Clone a configuration version, remove the policy you want to delete, then PUT the edited object back to Modify a security policy.List rate policy actions: All products Returns a list of all rate policies currently in use with the actions each policy takes when conditions are met.Modify a rate policy action: All products Updates the actions in a rate policy.Get IP/Geo Firewall settings: All products Lists which network lists are used in the IP/Geo Firewall settings. In Control Center this method is called mode. In this API the method is called blocked. The response shows blocked and allowed IPs depending on which network lists you include and which version of the mode you choose. If you want to add or remove IP addresses from the network lists, use the Network Lists API. Note that subnet controls are a legacy item in Control Center and are not available through this API.Modify IP/Geo Firewall settings: All products Update the method and which network lists to use for IP/Geo firewall blocking. In Control Center this method is called mode. In this API the method is called blocked. Use blockSpecificIPGeo to block any IPs, geographies, or network lists you choose with this setting. Use blockAllTrafficExceptAllowedIPs to allow specific IPs or geographies that you choose to let through while the rest remain blocked. IPs you want to allow are contained in the allowedIPNetworkLists. It's important to verify the IPs you block are the ones you intend to block as it's easy to block wanted traffic by accident. Note that subnet controls are a legacy item in Control Center and are not available through this API.Get attack payload logging settings for a policy: All products List a security policy's settings for attack payload logging. Attack payload logging is on by default, and in most cases you should leave it enabled. When set to NONE, the request body and response body appear as redacted in the log. For example, JSON_PAIRS:redacted. This operation applies at the security policy level, and overrides the attack payload logging settings at the configuration level on a per-policy basis.Modify attack payload logging settings for a policy: All products Update attack payload logging settings for a specific policy. This operation applies at the security policy level, and overrides the attack payload logging settings at the configuration level on a per-policy basis. When set to NONE, the request body and response body appear as redacted in the log. For example, JSON_PAIRS:redacted.Get HTTP header log settings: All products List a security policy's settings for HTTP header logging. HTTP header logging is on by default, and in most cases you should leave it enabled. You can filter requests by header type, including or excluding requests with a specific header, or by cookie. This operation applies at the security policy level, and overrides the HTTP header log settings at the configuration level on a per-policy basis.Modify HTTP header log settings: All products Enable, disable, or update HTTP header logging settings for a specific policy. This operation applies at the security policy level, and overrides the HTTP header log settings at the configuration level on a per-policy basis.List reputation profile actions: Kona Site Defender, App & API Protector with the Advanced Security module Return a list of reputation profiles with their associated actions.Get the action for a reputation profile: Kona Site Defender, App & API Protector with the Advanced Security module Return the action a reputation profile takes when triggered.Modify the action for a reputation profile: Kona Site Defender, App & API Protector with the Advanced Security module Update what action to take when reputation profile's rule triggers. Use alert to record the trigger of the event, deny to block the request, or none to take no action. Currently the only field in the reputation profile object is action.List custom rule actions: All products Returns a list of all configured custom rules for the specified configuration. It includes information for rules that are associated with this policy, as well as the latest versions of the rules in the configuration that aren't associated with the current policy. Unassociated rules have an action of none.Modify a custom rule action: All products Updates the action of a custom rule.Get reputation analysis settings: Kona Site Defender Return the current reputation analysis settings.Modify reputation analysis settings: Kona Site Defender Toggle the forwardToHTTPHeader and forwardSharedIPToHTTPHeaderAndSIEM options. The forwardToHTTPHeader option adds client reputation details to requests forwarded to origin in an HTTP header. The forwardSharedIPToHTTPHeaderAndSIEM option adds a value indicating that shared IPs are included in HTTP header and SIEM integration when used.List URL protection policy actions: All products Returns a list of all URL protection policies currently in use, along with the actions each policy takes when conditions are met.Modify a URL protection policy action: All products Updates the actions in a URL protection policy.Get Pragma settings for a security policy: All products Return the Pragma header's excluded conditions. By default, the Pragma header debugging information is stripped from an operation's response except in cases where you set excludeCondition. This operation applies at the security policy level. To modify Pragma header settings at the security configuration level, run List Pragma header settings for a configuration.Modify Pragma settings for a security policy: All products Update the pragma header excluded conditions. By default, the Pragma header debugging information is stripped from an operation's response except in cases where you set excludeCondition. To remove existing settings, submit your request with an empty payload {} at the top-level of an object. For example, submit "type": "{}" in the request body to remove the requestHeaderValueMatch from the excluded conditions. If you submit an empty payload for each field, you'll clear all of your condition settings. To modify Pragma header settings at the security configuration level, run Modify Pragma header settings for a configuration .List API request constraints and actions: Kona Site Defender, App & API Protector with the Advanced Security module Return a list of APIs with their constraints and associated actions.Modify the request constraint action for all APIs: Kona Site Defender, App & API Protector with the Advanced Security module Update what action to take when any API request constraint triggers. Use alert to record the trigger of the event, deny to block the request, or customDenyId to apply a custom deny response.Modify an API request constraint's action: Kona Site Defender, App & API Protector with the Advanced Security module Update what action to take when the API request constraint triggers. This operation modifies an individual API constraint action. To use this operation, run List all API request constraints and actions and pick an API from the response list. Use alert to record the trigger of the event, deny to block the request, or none to take no action. Currently the only field in the API Request Constraints object is action.Get evasive path match settings: Web Application Protector, Kona Site Defender Lists the evasive path match setting for a security policy. Evasive path match is off by default. This setting applies at the security policy level and overrides the setting at the configuration level on a per-policy basis.Modify evasive path match settings: Web Application Protector, Kona Site Defender Enable, disable, or update evasive path match setting for a security policy. This operation applies at the security policy level and overrides the setting at the configuration level on a per-policy basis.List malware policy actions: All products Return a list of all malware policies currently in use with the actions each policy takes when conditions are met.Modify a malware policy action: All products Update the actions in a malware policy.Get request body inspection limit settings for a security policy: All products Return request body inspection limit settings for a security policy. Contact your account team if you'd like to run this operation.Modify request body size settings for a security policy: All products Update inspection settings for a security policy. Inspect request bodies up to a certain size. In exceptional cases, you can change the default value to a set limit: 8, 16, or 32 KB. Contact your account team if you'd like to run this operation.List API endpoints: Kona Site Defender, App & API Protector with the Advanced Security module List the API endpoints associated with a security policy. This operation only lists the endpoints. To manage them, use Register an endpoint from the API Endpoint Definition API.Get slow POST protection settings: All products Get slow POST protection settings for a specific policy.Modify slow POST protection settings: All products Update slow POST protection settings for a specific policy.List rules: Kona Site Defender, App & API Protector with the Advanced Security module Returns the action taken for each rule in a policy. The action occurs when the rules are triggered by a request. These are not the same rules as Custom Rules that you configure yourself. These rules are maintained by Akamai.Upgrade KRS ruleset: Kona Site Defender, App & API Protector with the Advanced Security module, Adaptive Security Engine Upgrade to the most recent version of the KRS rule set. Akamai periodically updates these rules to keep protections current. However, the rules you use in your security policies do not automatically upgrade to the latest version when setting mode to KRS. These rules do update automatically when you have mode set to AAG. Before you upgrade, run Get upgrade details to see which rules have changed. If you want to test how these rules would operate with live traffic before committing to the upgrade, run them in evaluation mode. This applies to KRS rules only and does not allow you to make any changes to the rules themselves. The response is the same as the mode response. If you're already using or want to switch from KRS to Adaptive Security Engine (ASE), pass "upgrade": true, and "mode": "ASE_AUTO" or ASE_MANUAL in your request. If you're using Kona Rule Sets, continue to pass only the upgrade value. Note that this operation does not grant access to Adaptive Security Engine. It updates the ASE protections if you already have ASE on your contract. Once you switch to ASE protections, you can't go back to KRS rules. Contact your account team if you want to add ASE to your contract.Get upgrade details: Kona Site Defender, App & API Protector with the Advanced Security module Only applies to Kona rule sets. The KRS rule sets are maintained by Akamai's security research team. Run this operation before you upgrade to verify changes in the rule sets. If you want to test how the updates affect your site, you can run the updated rules in evaluation mode.Get the action for a rule: Kona Site Defender, App & API Protector with the Advanced Security module Return the action a rule takes when triggered. This applies to both ASE auto and ASE manual upgrade modes. Rule actions for ASE_AUTO are currently in beta. Contact your account team to access this option.Modify the action for a rule: Kona Site Defender, App & API Protector with the Advanced Security module Update what action a rule takes when it's triggered. This applies to both ASE auto and ASE manual upgrade modes. Rule actions for ASE_AUTO are currently in beta. Contact your account team to access this option. Use alert to record the trigger of the event, deny to block the request, or none to take no action.Get the conditions and exceptions of a rule: Kona Site Defender, App & API Protector with the Advanced Security module List a KRS rule's conditions and exceptions.Modify the conditions and exceptions of a rule: Kona Site Defender, App & API Protector with the Advanced Security module Update a rule's conditions and exceptions. When the conditions are met, the rule's actions are ignored and not applied to that specific traffic.Get adaptive intelligence settings: All products Returns whether adaptive intelligence is enabled. Adaptive intelligence allows our network to better tune rules for better accuracy. Contact your account team if you'd like to run this operation.Modify adaptive intelligence settings: All products Only applies to Adaptive Security Engine (ASE) manual rule sets. Enable or disable adaptive intelligence. Contact your account team if you'd like to run this operation.Get a security policy's rule set: All products Returns the security policy rule set, which includes the version, threat intelligence settings, rules, and attack group details.Modify a security policy's rule set: All products Modify the security policy's rule set including its rule and attack group details.Get protections: All products Get the protections and whether they are enabled or disabled in a security policy.Modify protections: All products Update the security policy protections. This applies a set of protections that you can enable individually.Get the penalty box: All products Returns the penalty box settings for the security policy you specify.Modify the penalty box: All products Modifies the penalty box settings for a security policy. When the penalty box is enabled for a policy, clients that trigger a WAF Deny action are placed in the penalty box. There, the action you select for penalty box (either Alert or Deny) continues to apply to any requests from that client for the next 10 minutes.Get penalty box condition: All products Returns the penalty box condition settings for a security policy.Modify the penalty box conditions: All products Modifies the penalty box conditions settings for a security policy.Respond to exception recommendations: Adaptive Security Engine Accept, decline, or reset the recommended exception. Accepting a tuning recommendation creates or updates the exception for the attack group. Use reset to restore a declined recommendation to a neutral state so you can accept it or decline it again later.Get tuning recommendations for a policy: Adaptive Security Engine Lists available tuning recommendations for a policy. Our system can identify patterns of false positives, and suggests exceptions for you to include in your policy.List tuning recommendations for an attack group: Adaptive Security Engine Returns available tuning recommendations for an attack group. Our system can identify patterns of false positives, and suggests exceptions for you to include in your attack group.List tuning recommendations for a rule: Adaptive Security Engine Returns available tuning recommendations for a rule. Our system can identify patterns of false positives, and suggests exceptions for you to include in your rule. In cases where your rules are already optimum, the response payload returns empty.List attack groups for a policy: All products Return a list of attack groups with their associated actions.Get the action for an attack group: All products Currently the only field in the response object is action, which displays the action for the attack group.Modify the action for an attack group: All products Update what action to take when an attack group's rule triggers. Use alert to record the trigger of the event, deny to block the request, or none to take no action. Currently the only field in the attack group object is action.Get the exceptions of an attack group: All products List an attack group's exceptions.Modify the exceptions of an attack group: All products Update an attack group exceptions.Get the current mode: All products When using Web Application Firewall in your security policy, this mode conveys how you're planning to keep the rules up to date, either KRS for manual updates or AAG for automatic updates. This operation returns which mode your rules are currently set to.Modify the mode: Kona Site Defender, App & API Protector with the Advanced Security module, Adaptive Security Engine The mode you set determines how your rule sets are updated. Use KRS mode to update the rule sets manually, or AAG to have them update automatically. If you're using Adaptive Security Engine, use ASE_AUTO to update the rules automatically, or ASE_MANUAL to update them yourself.List rapid rules: All products Returns rapid rules. Rapid rules are WAF rules we are actively testing and refining. You can start using them while we revise them. Once we complete fine-tuning a rule, it becomes a WAF rule you can access through List rules.Get rapid rules' default action: All products Returns the default action set for all rapid rules. To override this setting for an individual rule, run Update a rapid rule's action.Update rapid rules' default action: All products Set rapid rules default action. This applies to all rapid rules by default unless you specifically override this setting for an individual rule with Update a rapid rule's action.Get rapid rules' status: All products Returns whether rapid rules are enabled or disabled.Update rapid rules' status: All products Enable or disable all rapid rules.List a rapid rule's conditions and exceptions: All products Returns the conditions and exceptions set for the rapid rule.Update a rapid rule's conditions and exceptions: All products Set the rapid rule's conditions and exceptions.Get a rapid rule's lock status: All products Returns the rapid rule lock status. When locked, the action set for the rapid rule applies to all new versions of that rule.Update a rapid rule's lock status: All products Set the rapid rule lock status. When enabled, the action set for the rapid rule applies to all new versions of that rule.Get a rapid rule's action: All products Returns the action for a single rapid rule. Run Update a rapid rule's action if you want to set different actions for each rule, or override the default action for a single rule.Update a rapid rule's action: All products Set the rapid rule's action. Run this operation if you want to set different actions for each rule, or override the default action for a single rule.List AI rules: All products Returns all AI rules for the security policy. AI rules are WAF rules generated and refined using machine learning.Get AI rules status: All products Returns whether AI rules are enabled for the security policy.Update AI rules status: All products Enable or disable all AI rules for the security policy.Get an AI rule's action: All products Returns the action for the specified AI rule.Update an AI rule's action: All products Update the action for an AI rule.Create a challenge action: Create a new challenge action. Use this action type to insert a challenge, like a CAPTCHA, into the user workflow. You can also apply your own branding to the action to match your website. See Challenge actions for more details.List challenge actions: List all of your challenge actions along with their names, challenge types, and other summary information.Get a challenge action: View details about the specified challenge action.Update a challenge action: Edit the specified challenge action, such as the name, type of challenge, or branding.Delete a challenge action: Remove the specified challenge action.Update Google reCAPTCHA secret key: Specify a different Google reCAPTCHA secret key for a challenge action. The secret key authorizes communication between your site and the reCAPTCHA server.List Behavioral DDoS profile actions: Returns a list of all Behavioral DDoS profiles currently in use, along with the actions each profile takes when conditions are met. Products: All.Modify a Behavioral DDoS profile action: Updates the actions in a Behavioral DDoS profile. Products: All.Get the bypass network lists settings for a security policy: Web Application Protector, App & API Protector Lists which network lists are used in the bypass network lists settings. If you want to add or remove IP addresses from the network lists, use the Network Lists API.Modify the bypass network lists settings for a security policy: Web Application Protector, App & API Protector Update which network lists to use in the bypass network lists settings. If you want to add or remove IP addresses from the network lists, use the Network Lists API.Get Client-Side Protection & Compliance settings: All products Get Client-Side Protection & Compliance settings for a specific policy. For more information, see Client-side Protection & ComplianceModify Client-Side Protections & Compliance settings: All products Update Client-Side Protection & Compliance settings for a specific policy.List selected hostnames for a security policy: Web Application Protector, App & API Protector List the hostnames that the configuration version selects as candidates of protected hostnames, which you can use in match targets.Modify selected hostnames for a security policy: Web Application Protector, App & API Protector Update the list of selected hostnames for a configuration. You can add an individual hostname to your selected hostnames list without passing the entire list plus the new hostname in this PUT object.
